sanskrit: tvaṃ tu kevalam astrajño vīravratam anuṣṭhitaḥ śāstrārthaṃ tattvato gantuṃ na samarthaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: But you are versed in weapons alone, faithful to the vow of a warrior; you are in no way able to penetrate the meaning of the scriptures to its very truth.

sanskrit: śāstrārthasūkṣmadarśī yo dharmaniścayakovidaḥ tenāpy evaṃ na vācyo 'haṃ yadi dharmaṃ prapaśyasi
english: Even by one who discerns the subtle meaning of scripture and is skilled in the settled truths of dharma, I should not be addressed thus—if indeed you truly perceive dharma.

sanskrit: bhrātṛsauhṛdam āsthāya yad uktaṃ vacanaṃ tvayā nyāyyaṃ yuktaṃ ca kaunteya prīto 'haṃ tena te 'rjuna
english: Yet the words you have spoken, resting on a brother's affection, are reasonable and fitting, O son of Kuntī; for that I am pleased with you, Arjuna.

sanskrit: yuddhadharmeṣu sarveṣu kriyāṇāṃ naipuṇeṣu ca na tvayā sadṛśaḥ kaś cit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate
english: In all the duties of war and in every skill of action, no one your equal is to be found in the three worlds.

sanskrit: dharmasūkṣmaṃ tu yad vākyaṃ tatra duṣprataraṃ tvayā dhanaṃjaya na me buddhim abhiśaṅkitum arhasi
english: But where the subtle teaching of dharma is concerned, that ground is hard for you to cross over, Dhanaṃjaya; you ought not to call my understanding into doubt.

sanskrit: yuddhaśāstravid eva tvaṃ na vṛddhāḥ sevitās tvayā samāsavistaravidāṃ na teṣāṃ vetsi niścayam
english: You know only the science of war; you have not waited upon the elders, and you do not grasp the considered conclusions of those who know matters both in brief and at length.

sanskrit: tapas tyāgo vidhir iti niścayas tāta dhīmatām paraṃ paraṃ jyāya eṣāṃ saiṣā naiḥśreyasī gatiḥ
english: Austerity, renunciation, and right observance—such is the settled view of the wise, dear one; each of these is higher and more excellent than the last, and this is the path that leads to the supreme good.

sanskrit: na tv etan manyase pārtha na jyāyo 'sti dhanād iti atra te vartayiṣyāmi yathā naitat pradhānataḥ
english: But you do not hold to this, Pārtha; you say there is nothing higher than wealth. On this I shall set you right, showing how wealth is not the foremost thing.

sanskrit: tapaḥsvādhyāyaśīlā hi dṛśyante dhārmikā janāḥ ṛṣayas tapasā yuktā yeṣāṃ lokāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: For righteous folk are seen given to austerity and to the study of sacred lore, sages joined to austerity, whose worlds are everlasting.

sanskrit: ajātaśmaśravo dhīrās tathānye vanavāsinaḥ anantā adhanā eva svādhyāyena divaṃ gatāḥ
english: Steadfast men whose beards had not yet grown, and others dwelling in the forest, countless and wholly without wealth, have gone to heaven by the study of the sacred word.

sanskrit: uttareṇa tu panthānam āryā viṣayanigrahāt abuddhijaṃ tamas tyaktvā lokāṃs tyāgavatāṃ gatāḥ
english: By the northern path the noble ones, through the restraint of the senses, casting off the darkness born of unwisdom, have reached the worlds of those who renounce.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇena tu panthānaṃ yaṃ bhāsvantaṃ prapaśyasi ete kriyāvatāṃ lokā ye śmaśānāni bhejire
english: But that shining path you behold to the south—these are the worlds of men of ritual action, who have resorted to the cremation grounds.

sanskrit: anirdeśyā gatiḥ sā tu yāṃ prapaśyanti mokṣiṇaḥ tasmāt tyāgaḥ pradhāneṣṭaḥ sa tu duḥkhaḥ praveditum
english: But indescribable is that goal which the seekers of liberation behold; therefore renunciation is held the foremost good, though it is hard to make known.

sanskrit: anusṛtya tu śāstrāṇi kavayaḥ samavasthitāḥ apīha syād apīha syāt sārāsāradidṛkṣayā
english: Following the scriptures, the wise have taken their stand, asking 'might it be thus here, might it be thus,' in their longing to discern the essence from the dross.

sanskrit: vedavādān atikramya śāstrāṇy āraṇyakāni ca vipāṭya kadalīskandhaṃ sāraṃ dadṛśire na te
english: Going beyond the doctrines of the Vedas and the forest treatises, they split open the plantain trunk—and found in it no pith at all.

sanskrit: athaikāntavyudāsena śarīre pañcabhautike icchādveṣasamāyuktam ātmānaṃ prāhur iṅgitaiḥ
english: Then, by sheer process of exclusion, within the body made of the five elements they declared, by inference from its signs, a Self joined with desire and aversion.

sanskrit: agrāhyaś cakṣuṣā so 'pi anirdeśyaṃ ca tad girā karmahetupuraskāraṃ bhūteṣu parivartate
english: He cannot be grasped by the eye, and That cannot be pointed out by speech; impelled by the force of past deeds, He revolves through living beings.

sanskrit: kalyāṇagocaraṃ kṛtvā manas tṛṣṇāṃ nigṛhya ca karmasaṃtatim utsṛjya syān nirālambanaḥ sukhī
english: Having made the mind range over what is good and curbed all craving, casting off the unbroken stream of action, one may become free of every support and happy.

sanskrit: asminn evaṃ sūkṣmagamye mārge sadbhir niṣevite katham artham anarthāḍhyam arjuna tvaṃ praśaṃsasi
english: When such is the path, attainable only by subtle insight and trodden by the good, how, Arjuna, can you praise wealth, which is so full of harm?

sanskrit: pūrvaśāstravido hy evaṃ janāḥ paśyanti bhārata kriyāsu niratā nityaṃ dāne yajñe ca karmaṇi
english: For thus do men learned in the ancient scriptures see it, O Bhārata—men ever devoted to ritual acts, to giving, to sacrifice, and to works.

sanskrit: bhavanti sudurāvartā hetumanto 'pi paṇḍitāḥ dṛḍhapūrvaśrutā mūḍhā naitad astīti vādinaḥ
english: There are men hard to turn aside, learned and full of arguments, yet fixed in the lore they first heard, deluded, declaring 'this does not exist.'

sanskrit: amṛtasyāvamantāro vaktāro janasaṃsadi caranti vasudhāṃ kṛtsnāṃ vāvadūkā bahuśrutāḥ
english: Scorners of the immortal truth, holding forth in the assemblies of men, they wander the whole earth, voluble and widely read.

sanskrit: yān vayaṃ nābhijānīmaḥ kas tāñ jñātum ihārhati evaṃ prājñān sataś cāpi mahataḥ śāstravittamān
english: Whom even we do not fully understand—who here is fit to understand them, men so wise, so true, so great, the foremost in knowledge of scripture?

sanskrit: tapasā mahad āpnoti buddhyā vai vindate mahat tyāgena sukham āpnoti sadā kaunteya dharmavit
english: By austerity one attains greatness; by wisdom one finds what is great; by renunciation the knower of dharma ever wins happiness, O son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin vākyāntare vaktā devasthāno mahātapāḥ abhinītataraṃ vākyam ity uvāca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At this break in the discourse, the eloquent Devasthāna of mighty austerities spoke these well-fashioned words to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yad vacaḥ phalgunenoktaṃ na jyāyo 'sti dhanād iti atra te vartayiṣyāmi tad ekāgramanāḥ śṛṇu
english: The words spoken by Phalguna—that there is nothing higher than wealth—on these I shall set you right; hear it with single-minded attention.

sanskrit: ajātaśatro dharmeṇa kṛtsnā te vasudhā jitā tāṃ jitvā na vṛthā rājaṃs tvaṃ parityaktum arhasi
english: O Ajātaśatru, by righteousness the whole earth has been won by you; having won it, you ought not, O king, to cast it away in vain.

sanskrit: catuṣpadī hi niḥśreṇī karmaṇy eṣā pratiṣṭhitā tāṃ krameṇa mahābāho yathāvaj jaya pārthiva
english: A four-runged ladder it is, established upon action; mount it rung by rung, mighty-armed king, in due order.

sanskrit: tasmāt pārtha mahāyajñair yajasva bahudakṣiṇaiḥ svādhyāyayajñā ṛṣayo jñānayajñās tathāpare
english: Therefore, Pārtha, sacrifice with great sacrifices rich in priestly gifts; some sages sacrifice by sacred study, and others by the sacrifice of knowledge.

sanskrit: karmaniṣṭhāṃs tu budhyethās taponiṣṭhāṃś ca bhārata vaikhānasānāṃ rājendra vacanaṃ śrūyate yathā
english: Know that some are steadfast in works and some steadfast in austerity, O Bhārata; for so, O king of kings, runs the teaching of the Vaikhānasa hermits.

sanskrit: īhate dhanahetor yas tasyānīhā garīyasī bhūyān doṣaḥ pravardheta yas taṃ dhanam apāśrayet
english: For one who strives for the sake of wealth, not striving would be the weightier good; greater fault would grow in the man who leaned upon that wealth.

sanskrit: kṛcchrāc ca dravyasaṃhāraṃ kurvanti dhanakāraṇāt dhanena tṛṣito 'buddhyā bhrūṇahatyāṃ na budhyate
english: With great toil men amass goods for the sake of wealth; and one athirst for wealth, in his folly, does not even perceive the slaying of an unborn child.

sanskrit: anarhate yad dadāti na dadāti yad arhate anarhārhāparijñānād dānadharmo 'pi duṣkaraḥ
english: He gives to the unworthy, and gives not to the worthy; for want of discerning the unworthy from the worthy, even the duty of giving is hard to fulfill.

sanskrit: yajñāya sṛṣṭāni dhanāni dhātrā; yaṣṭādiṣṭaḥ puruṣo rakṣitā ca tasmāt sarvaṃ yajña evopayojyaṃ; dhanaṃ tato 'nantara eva kāmaḥ
english: Riches were created by the Ordainer for sacrifice, and man was ordained the sacrificer and the guardian; therefore all wealth is to be employed in sacrifice alone, and only thereafter desire.

sanskrit: yajñair indro vividhair annavadbhir; devān sarvān abhyayān mahaujāḥ tenendratvaṃ prāpya vibhrājate 'sau; tasmād yajñe sarvam evopayojyam
english: By manifold sacrifices laden with offerings of food, Indra of mighty power surpassed all the gods; having thereby gained the rank of Indra he shines forth—therefore all is to be employed in sacrifice.

sanskrit: mahādevaḥ sarvamedhe mahātmā; hutvātmānaṃ devadevo vibhūtaḥ viśvāṃl lokān vyāpya viṣṭabhya kīrtyā; virocate dyutimān kṛttivāsāḥ
english: The great-souled Mahādeva, god of gods, in the all-sacrifice offered up his very Self and so became glorious; pervading and upholding all the worlds with his fame, the radiant one clad in a hide shines resplendent.

sanskrit: āvikṣitaḥ pārthivo vai maruttaḥ; svṛddhyā martyo yo 'jayad devarājam yajñe yasya śrīḥ svayaṃ saṃniviṣṭā; yasmin bhāṇḍaṃ kāñcanaṃ sarvam āsīt
english: Marutta, the son of Avikṣit, a king and a mortal, by his abundance overcame the lord of the gods; in his sacrifice Royal Splendor herself took up her seat, and where every vessel was of gold.

sanskrit: hariścandraḥ pārthivendraḥ śrutas te; yajñair iṣṭvā puṇyakṛd vītaśokaḥ ṛddhyā śakraṃ yo 'jayan mānuṣaḥ saṃs; tasmād yajñe sarvam evopayojyam
english: Hariścandra, lord among kings, of whom you have heard—by sacrifices he worshipped, a doer of merit, freed from sorrow; though a man, by his prosperity he surpassed Śakra—therefore all is to be employed in sacrifice.

sanskrit: devasthāna uvāca atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam indreṇa samaye pṛṣṭo yad uvāca bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Devasthāna said: On this very matter they recount this ancient tale—what Bṛhaspati, when questioned in due season by Indra, answered.

sanskrit: saṃtoṣo vai svargatamaḥ saṃtoṣaḥ paramaṃ sukham tuṣṭer na kiṃ cit parataḥ susamyak paritiṣṭhati
english: Contentment is the very height of heaven; contentment is the supreme happiness; nothing stands more firmly and rightly established than satisfaction.

sanskrit: yadā saṃharate kāmān kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ tadātmajyotir ātmaiva svātmanaiva prasīdati
english: When a man draws in his desires from every side, as a tortoise draws in its limbs, then the Self, self-luminous, grows serene through its own self alone.

sanskrit: na bibheti yadā cāyaṃ yadā cāsmān na bibhyati kāmadveṣau ca jayati tadātmānaṃ prapaśyati
english: When he fears nothing and nothing fears him, and he conquers desire and aversion, then he beholds the Self.

sanskrit: yadāsau sarvabhūtānāṃ na krudhyati na duṣyati karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When toward all beings he neither rages nor bears ill will, then in deed, in thought, and in word he attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: evaṃ kaunteya bhūtāni taṃ taṃ dharmaṃ tathā tathā tadā tadā prapaśyanti tasmād budhyasva bhārata
english: Thus, O son of Kuntī, beings perceive this dharma and that, each in its own way and in its own time; understand this therefore, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: anye śamaṃ praśaṃsanti vyāyāmam apare tathā naikaṃ na cāparaṃ ke cid ubhayaṃ ca tathāpare
english: Some praise tranquillity, others again exertion; some praise neither the one nor the other, and others still praise both together.

sanskrit: yajñam eke praśaṃsanti saṃnyāsam apare janāḥ dānam eke praśaṃsanti ke cid eva pratigraham ke cit sarvaṃ parityajya tūṣṇīṃ dhyāyanta āsate
english: Some men praise sacrifice, others renunciation; some praise giving, while certain ones praise receiving; and some, abandoning all, sit silent in meditation.

sanskrit: rājyam eke praśaṃsanti sarveṣāṃ paripālanam hatvā bhittvā ca chittvā ca ke cid ekāntaśīlinaḥ
english: Some praise kingship and the protection of all, slaying, smiting, and cutting down; while certain ones live in utter solitude.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ samālokya budhānām eṣa niścayaḥ adroheṇaiva bhūtānāṃ yo dharmaḥ sa satāṃ mataḥ
english: Surveying all this, the considered judgment of the wise is this: the dharma that lies in doing no harm to living beings is the one esteemed by the good.

sanskrit: adrohaḥ satyavacanaṃ saṃvibhāgo dhṛtiḥ kṣamā prajanaḥ sveṣu dāreṣu mārdavaṃ hrīr acāpalam
english: Harmlessness, truthful speech, fair sharing, steadfastness, forbearance, the begetting of children upon one's own wife, gentleness, modesty, and freedom from fickleness—

sanskrit: dhanaṃ dharmapradhāneṣṭaṃ manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt tasmād evaṃ prayatnena kaunteya paripālaya
english: wealth whose chief aim is dharma—so Manu, son of the Self-existent, declared; therefore, O son of Kuntī, govern thus with every effort.

sanskrit: yo hi rājye sthitaḥ śaśvad vaśī tulyapriyāpriyaḥ kṣatriyo yajñaśiṣṭāśī rājaśāstrārthatattvavit
english: For the kṣatriya who stands firm in kingship, ever self-controlled, the same toward what is dear and not dear, eating the remnants of sacrifice, knowing the true meaning of the science of statecraft—

sanskrit: asādhunigraharataḥ sādhūnāṃ pragrahe rataḥ dharme vartmani saṃsthāpya prajā varteta dharmavit
english: intent on curbing the wicked, intent on the advancement of the good—such a knower of dharma should rule, having set his subjects firmly on the path of righteousness.

sanskrit: putrasaṃkrāmitaśrīs tu vane vanyena vartayan vidhinā śrāmaṇenaiva kuryāt kālam atandritaḥ
english: Then, having passed his royal fortune on to his son, dwelling in the forest and living on its wild produce, by the rule of the ascetics, unwearied, let him await his appointed hour.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ vartate rājā rājadharmaviniścitaḥ tasyāyaṃ ca paraś caiva lokaḥ syāt saphalo nṛpa nirvāṇaṃ tu suduṣpāraṃ bahuvighnaṃ ca me matam
english: The king who lives thus, resolved in the dharma of kings—for him both this world and the next shall be fruitful, O lord of men; but liberation, in my view, is very hard to reach and beset with many obstacles.

sanskrit: evaṃ dharmam anukrāntāḥ satyadānatapaḥparāḥ ānṛśaṃsyaguṇair yuktāḥ kāmakrodhavivarjitāḥ
english: Thus pursuing dharma, devoted to truth, giving, and austerity, endowed with the virtues of compassion, free of desire and wrath—

sanskrit: prajānāṃ pālane yuktā damam uttamam āsthitāḥ gobrāhmaṇārthaṃ yuddhena saṃprāptā gatim uttamām
english: intent on the protection of their subjects, established in the highest self-restraint—through battle waged for the sake of cattle and brāhmaṇas they have attained the supreme goal.

sanskrit: evaṃ rudrāḥ savasavas tathādityāḥ paraṃtapa sādhyā rājarṣisaṃghāś ca dharmam etaṃ samāśritāḥ apramattās tataḥ svargaṃ prāptāḥ puṇyaiḥ svakarmabhiḥ
english: Thus the Rudras together with the Vasus, and the Ādityas too, O scorcher of foes, the Sādhyas, and the bands of royal sages, taking refuge in this dharma, vigilant, attained heaven thereafter by their own meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin vākyāntare vākyaṃ punar evārjuno 'bravīt viṣaṇṇamanasaṃ jyeṣṭham idaṃ bhrātaram īśvaram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At this break in the discourse Arjuna spoke again these words to his eldest brother, the lord whose mind was sunk in despondency.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmeṇa dharmajña prāpya rājyam anuttamam jitvā cārīn naraśreṣṭha tapyate kiṃ bhavān bhṛśam
english: Having gained an unrivalled kingdom by the dharma of a kṣatriya, O knower of dharma, and having conquered your foes, O best of men, why do you grieve so bitterly?

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahārāja saṃgrāme nidhanaṃ smṛtam viśiṣṭaṃ bahubhir yajñaiḥ kṣatradharmam anusmara
english: For kṣatriyas, O great king, death in battle is held to surpass many sacrifices; call to mind the dharma of the kṣatriya.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ tapas tyāgaḥ pretyadharmavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca vihitaṃ saṃgrāme nidhanaṃ vibho
english: For brāhmaṇas, austerity and renunciation are declared the ordained means to the world beyond; but for kṣatriyas, O lord, death in battle is appointed.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmo mahāraudraḥ śastranitya iti smṛtaḥ vadhaś ca bharataśreṣṭha kāle śastreṇa saṃyuge
english: The dharma of the kṣatriya is most fierce, ever bound to the sword, it is declared—and slaying too, O best of the Bharatas, with the weapon in battle at its proper hour.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasyāpi ced rājan kṣatradharmeṇa tiṣṭhataḥ praśastaṃ jīvitaṃ loke kṣatraṃ hi brahmasaṃsthitam
english: Even for a brāhmaṇa, O king, who abides by the dharma of the kṣatriya, life is praised in this world; for the kṣatriya order is grounded in the brahman.

sanskrit: na tyāgo na punar yācñā na tapo manujeśvara kṣatriyasya vidhīyante na parasvopajīvanam
english: Neither renunciation, nor begging, nor austerity, O lord of men, are ordained for the kṣatriya, nor living upon the goods of another.

sanskrit: sa bhavān sarvadharmajñaḥ sarvātmā bharatarṣabha rājā manīṣī nipuṇo loke dṛṣṭaparāvaraḥ
english: And you are the knower of all dharmas, devoted with your whole being, O bull of the Bharatas, a king, wise and skilled, who in this world has seen both the higher and the lower.

sanskrit: tyaktvā saṃtāpajaṃ śokaṃ daṃśito bhava karmaṇi kṣatriyasya viśeṣeṇa hṛdayaṃ vajrasaṃhatam
english: Cast off the grief born of anguish and gird yourself for action; the heart of a kṣatriya above all is hard as the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: jitvārīn kṣatradharmeṇa prāpya rājyam akaṇṭakam vijitātmā manuṣyendra yajñadānaparo bhava
english: Having conquered your foes by the dharma of the kṣatriya and gained a kingdom free of thorns, master of yourself, O lord of men, be devoted to sacrifice and to giving.

sanskrit: indro vai brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ karmaṇā kṣatriyo 'bhavat jñātīnāṃ pāpavṛttīnāṃ jaghāna navatīr nava
english: Indra was indeed the son of Brahmā, yet by his deeds he became a kṣatriya; of his kinsmen of wicked ways he slew nine times ninety.

sanskrit: tac cāsya karma pūjyaṃ hi praśasyaṃ ca viśāṃ pate tena cendratvam āpede devānām iti naḥ śrutam
english: And that deed of his is honored and praised, O lord of peoples; by it he attained the lordship of Indra over the gods—so have we heard.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ yajñair mahārāja yajasva bahudakṣiṇaiḥ yathaivendro manuṣyendra cirāya vigatajvaraḥ
english: So do you, O great king, sacrifice with sacrifices rich in priestly gifts, even as Indra did, O lord of men, your fever of grief long since departed.

sanskrit: mā tvam evaṃgate kiṃ cit kṣatriyarṣabha śocithāḥ gatās te kṣatradharmeṇa śastrapūtāḥ parāṃ gatim
english: Grieve not at all over what has come to pass, O bull among kṣatriyas; those who fell have gone, by the dharma of the kṣatriya and purified by the sword, to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: bhavitavyaṃ tathā tac ca yad vṛttaṃ bharatarṣabha diṣṭaṃ hi rājaśārdūla na śakyam ativartitum
english: What has come to pass had to be so, O bull of the Bharatas; for what is ordained, O tiger among kings, cannot be overstepped.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu kaunteyo guḍākeśena bhārata novāca kiṃ cit kauravyas tato dvaipāyano 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Guḍākeśa, the son of Kuntī, O Bhārata, the Kaurava said nothing at all; whereupon Dvaipāyana spoke.

sanskrit: bībhatsor vacanaṃ samyak satyam etad yudhiṣṭhira śāstradṛṣṭaḥ paro dharmaḥ smṛto gārhasthya āśramaḥ
english: The words of Bībhatsu are right, and this is true, Yudhiṣṭhira; the householder's stage of life is declared by scripture to be the supreme dharma.

sanskrit: svadharmaṃ cara dharmajña yathāśāstraṃ yathāvidhi na hi gārhasthyam utsṛjya tavāraṇyaṃ vidhīyate
english: Follow your own dharma, O knower of dharma, according to scripture and according to rule; for it is not ordained that you abandon the householder's life for the forest.

sanskrit: gṛhasthaṃ hi sadā devāḥ pitara ṛṣayas tathā bhṛtyāś caivopajīvanti tān bhajasva mahīpate
english: For upon the householder the gods, the ancestors, the sages, and his dependents ever live; cherish them, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: vayāṃsi paśavaś caiva bhūtāni ca mahīpate gṛhasthair eva dhāryante tasmāj jyeṣṭhāśramo gṛhī
english: Birds, beasts, and all creatures, O lord of the earth, are sustained by householders alone; therefore the householder's is the foremost stage of life.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ caturṇām eteṣām āśramāṇāṃ durācaraḥ taṃ carāvimanāḥ pārtha duścaraṃ durbalendriyaiḥ
english: This stage, of these four orders of life, is the hardest to follow; tread it, Pārtha, with a steady mind—hard to tread as it is for those whose senses are weak.

sanskrit: vedajñānaṃ ca te kṛtsnaṃ tapaś ca caritaṃ mahat pitṛpaitāmahe rājye dhuram udvoḍhum arhasi
english: Your knowledge of the Vedas is complete, and great austerity has been practiced by you; you ought now to bear the yoke of the kingdom of your fathers and forefathers.

sanskrit: tapo yajñas tathā vidyā bhaikṣam indriyanigrahaḥ dhyānam ekāntaśīlatvaṃ tuṣṭir dānaṃ ca śaktitaḥ
english: Austerity, sacrifice, and sacred learning, the life of alms, the curbing of the senses, meditation, the practice of solitude, contentment, and giving according to one's power—
